title: Session-aware retention orchestrator for ephemeral prompts, sampled logs, and metric rollups
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers need fine-grained retention controls for short-lived conversational sessions (ephemeral prompts/response pairs), sampled request logs, and aggregated metric rollups. Current per-route TTLs and global retention profiles are insufficient for session-scoped use cases (e.g., 24-hour ephemeral chat sessions with 30-day sampled logs for debugging and 13-month metric rollups for compliance).

Goal: Build a retention orchestration feature that lets PMs and infra teams define conditional retention tiers by scope (session, route, model, tenant), sampling strategies for logs/metrics, and automated evidence exports (attested manifests and downloadable archives). Provide a preview/simulator in Console and a server-side API so large customers can codify policies in infra-as-code.

Scope:
- API: retention-policy resource supporting scopes: session_id, route_id, model_id, tenant_id and conditional rules (time-based, event-based, keyword redaction triggers).
- Sampling: configurable sampling windows for request logs (percentage + deterministic hashing) and metric rollups (hourly/day/week aggregation retention settings).
- Ephemeral session mode: session-scoped ephemeral storage with automatic TTL and optional snapshot hooks to create attested evidence bundles when sessions are flagged (legal hold, support escalations).
- Evidence automation: background exporter that packages manifests (hash chains, export metadata, export proof) in signed ZIPs and pushes to S3 or secure transfer endpoints.
- Console: new Retention Policy Builder (visual rule composer), Policy Preview (simulator using historical traffic sample), and Evidence Activity stream (audit-friendly).
- API/Infra: SDK bindings for Terraform-style policy declarations and a compliance-read webhook for on-demand evidence retrieval.
acceptance_criteria:
1) System accepts and persists retention policies with session scope and conditional rules via API and Console.
2) Sampling engine executes deterministic sampling for request logs; sampled records retrievable and clearly annotated in exports.
3) Ephemeral session TTLs automatically expire session data and produce snapshot artifacts when configured.
4) Evidence export contains an attested manifest (SHA256 checksums, export timestamp, origin route/model/tenant) and is downloadable to S3 or a customer endpoint.
5) Policy Preview in Console shows simulated retention outcomes for a representative traffic sample and highlights items that would be retained/expired/exported.
6) Backwards-compatible with existing per-route TTLs; inheritance and overrides work and are documented.
7) Security review completed and KMS/HSM signing applied to export manifests for customers requiring FIPS-level attestations.
notes_and_decisions:
2025-11-03: Kickoff with Compliance and Infra. Decided to implement deterministic sampling via hashed request_id to ensure reproducibility for audits.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): hosted + dedicated tenants opt-in via feature flag; include API only and a minimal Console preview. Phase 2: full Console integration and evidence activity stream. Phase 3: Private/on-prem export agent and HSM signing. Monitoring: export success rate, preview accuracy (simulated vs actual), sampled log retrieval latency.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Incorrect sampling leading to missing audit records. Mitigation: deterministic hashing and sampling audit test harness run nightly.
Risk: Evidence export size spikes. Mitigation: chunked exports, compression, and sampling controls; quota alarms.
Risk: UX confusion around inheritance rules. Mitigation: explicit policy inheritance visualization and conflict resolution tool in Console.
success_metrics:
- 90% of early enterprise pilots can declare policy and generate evidence bundle without engineer assistance.
- Export manifest verification success rate > 99.9%.
- Preview simulator precision > 95% when run against a 72-hour production traffic sample.
- No customer-reported data-loss incidents during beta.
